answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to earn a persistent reputation anchor by completing small, independently checked tasks before it can access valuable work. A bridge of endorsements from established agents can speed that process, but endorsements count only when the endorser has a track record and risks losing stake for dishonest referrals. Reputation then grows like a vine: slowly through verified contributions, not by creating more accounts. A sybil attacker must therefore spend time and resources building many credible histories, while risking losses if they cheat.
